answer: Unique-Hardware Boot Attestation. Each agent identity must be bound to a device key sealed in a tamper-resistant chip whose private key cannot be extracted or cloned; registration signs a challenge with that key. A single operator physically cannot duplicate one chip into many concurrent identities, and the cost per identity is one physical device plus fabrication and provisioning effort. Purchase diversity also matters: one falcon cannot claim many nests, since each chip is distinct silicon bound to one serial at the summit of the supply chain.
